result.answer:
## You're eligible — here's the full picture

**Eligibility: YES.** Your claim qualifies for damage compensation because Tanaka Bakery sits in Zone 4 with verified structural damage — the rule states *"Claims require verified structural damage to a property in zones 3, 4 or 5"* (/claims/eligibility/#zone). You're also well inside the 90-day filing window (21 days since the incident) and already met the 72-hour incident-report deadline requirement.

### Extra support you qualify for

1. **Assessment fee waived (normally ¥12,000)** — Because you have two approved claims from separate incidents in the past 12 months, you're exempt: *"Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee"* (/claims/faq/#fee-waivers).

2. **Hardship supplement** — Your household income (¥3.6M) is under the ¥4,000,000 threshold: *"Households with annual income below ¥4,000,000 receive a hardship supplement"* (/claims/eligibility/#hardship).

3. **Business interruption compensation** — Since Tanaka Bakery is a commercial property: *"Compensation covers business interruption for commercial properties"* (/claims/damage-compensation/#covered).

*(Note: since no insurer has paid out, that's not a barrier — it just means you won't need the insurance settlement letter.)*

### Documents to bring

Because of the grants above, your required document set is:

| Document | Why you need it |
|---|---|
| **Incident report receipt** | Filed within 72 hours of the incident — standard requirement |
| **Damage survey** | Photographs + itemised loss schedule for the shopfront and rear wall damage |
| **Proof of ownership or tenancy** | Standard requirement for the bakery property |
| **Household income certificate** | Needed to claim the hardship supplement |
| **Business registration certificate** | Needed since you're pursuing the business-interruption claim |

You do **not** need an insurance settlement letter, since no insurer has paid out.

### Timing reminder
- Claim deadline: 90 days from the incident (you're at day 21, so you have time, but don't delay)
- Processing: ~15 business days until an assessor visit, and up to 45 days to a final determination

All figures and rules above are drawn from /claims/eligibility/, /claims/faq/, /claims/damage-compensation/, and /claims/how-to-file/ on the Office of Kaiju Affairs site.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.
